_meta.indication: ADUHELM is indicated for the treatment of Alzheimer's disease, approved under accelerated approval based on reduction in amyloid beta plaques observed in patients treated with ADUHELM.

pivotal_trials.design: Double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled, parallel group study; patients randomized 1:1:1 to ADUHELM low dose, ADUHELM high dose (10 mg/kg), or placebo every 4 weeks for 18 months.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with Alzheimer's disease with confirmed amyloid pathology and mild cognitive impairment or mild dementia stage (Stage 3 and Stage 4); CDR global score 0.5, RBANS delayed memory index score ≤ 85, and MMSE 24-30. Mean age 71 years (range 50-85).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline on the CDR-Sum of Boxes (CDR-SB) at Week 78.
pivotal_trials.n: 1638 patients randomized (high dose N=547, placebo N=548).
pivotal_trials.result: ADUHELM high dose demonstrated statistically significant reduction in clinical decline vs placebo on CDR-SB: difference from placebo -0.39 (-22%), p = 0.0120.

pivotal_trials.design: Double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled, parallel group study; patients randomized 1:1:1 to ADUHELM low dose, ADUHELM high dose (10 mg/kg), or placebo every 4 weeks for 18 months.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with Alzheimer's disease with confirmed amyloid pathology and mild cognitive impairment or mild dementia stage (Stage 3 and Stage 4); CDR global score 0.5, RBANS delayed memory index score ≤ 85, and MMSE 24-30. Mean age 71 years (range 50-85).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline in CDR-SB score at 78 weeks.
pivotal_trials.result: Negative study: no statistically significant differences between ADUHELM-treated and placebo-treated patients on the primary endpoint (change from baseline in CDR-SB at 78 weeks).

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥10% and higher than placebo) were ARIA-E, headache, ARIA-H microhemorrhage, ARIA-H superficial siderosis, and fall. In Table 3 (Studies 1 and 2, N=1105 ADUHELM 10 mg/kg vs N=1087 placebo): ARIA-E 35% vs 3%, headache 21% vs 16%, ARIA-H microhemorrhage 19% vs 7%, ARIA-H superficial siderosis 15% vs 2%, fall 15% vs 12%. ARIA (-E and/or -H) occurred in 41% of ADUHELM patients vs 10% placebo.
target_moa: Aducanumab-avwa is a human IgG1 monoclonal antibody directed against aggregated soluble and insoluble forms of amyloid beta; accumulation of amyloid beta plaques is a defining pathophysiological feature of Alzheimer's disease, and ADUHELM reduces amyloid beta plaques.

rems.type: FDA determined that, at this time, a REMS is not necessary for Aduhelm to ensure that its benefits outweigh its risks.

advisory_committee.vote: Peripheral and Central Nervous System Drugs Advisory Committee (November 6, 2020). On whether Study 302 provided strong evidence of effectiveness, the vote was Yes: 1, No: 8, Uncertain: 2; on considering Study 302 as primary evidence of effectiveness, Yes: 0, No: 10, Uncertain: 1.

description.text: Added clinical study data on plasma p-Tau 181 and updated ARIA-related labeling information (no new indication or population)

citations.quote: This Prior Approval sBLA provides for the addition of clinical study data regarding plasma p-Tau 181 to the Clinical Pharmacology (12.2) and Clinical Studies (14) sections of the Prescribing Information (PI). This sBLA also includes revisions throughout the PI (Dosage and Administration [2.1-2.5], Warnings and Precautions [5.1], Adverse Reactions [previously 6.2], and Patient Counseling Information [17]) that provide for updated information with respect to ARIA associated with the use of Aduhelm, clarification and reorganization of information already in the PI, and for consistency in labeling across the drug class. Updates were also made to Clinical Pharmacology [12.6] based on new guidance recommendations for immunogenicity1 and to Use in Specific Populations [8.2]. Revisions were included in the Medication Guide to align with revisions in the PI.

surrogate_endpoint.text: Reduction in amyloid beta plaques (measured by PET), an endpoint considered reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit.

citations.quote: This indication is approved under accelerated approval based on reduction in amyloid beta plaques observed in patients treated with ADUHELM [see Clinical Studies (14)].
The critical question is whether reduction in brain amyloid plaque as measured by PET is an endpoint that is reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit.

confirmatory_requirement.text: PMR 3971-1: conduct a randomized, controlled trial to verify the clinical benefit of aducanumab compared to an appropriate control for the treatment of Alzheimer's disease.

The trial should be of sufficient duration to observe changes on an acceptable endpoint in the patient population enrolled in the trial.

summary.text: BLA 761178 was received July 7, 2020 and given Priority review. It was approved June 7, 2021 under the accelerated approval regulations (21 CFR 601.41) based on reduction in amyloid beta plaques, an endpoint reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit, with a required confirmatory trial (PMR 3971-1) to verify clinical benefit. Two prior requests for breakthrough therapy designation had been denied. An advisory committee voted overwhelmingly against the strength of the effectiveness evidence.
